To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fluoroquinolone therapy for enteric fever in adults is associated with a reduction in clinical relapse compared with chloramphenical and is associated with a lower rate of clinical failure compared with cefixim.
Fluoroquinolone antibiotics are effective for the treatment of typhoid and are better than chloram-phenicol at preventing relapse of the disease in adults.

1) fluoroquinolone treatment is not inferior to chloramphenicol or azithromycine for treating enteric fevers; 2) fluoroquinone treatment reduces clinical failure compared to ceftriaxon or cefixime; 3) fluoroquinoline treatment is not inferior compared to cefixime in children with nalidix acid-resistant strains.
